Marathon Petroleum is up 0.31% today and has gained 7.81% over the past two weeks—a climb that tracks closely with rising oil prices and tightening global refining capacity. US crude hit $91.48 a barrel and refineries are running at 98% utilization, their highest operating rate, while diesel prices have hit record highs as Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries and Iran sanctions have knocked out competing capacity. For a refiner like Marathon, higher crude prices and constrained competition mean wider profit margins on every gallon of fuel produced.

The geopolitical backdrop has shifted sharply in the refiner's favor. The U.S. deal with Venezuela, new EU sanctions on Iran, and military efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz all point toward sustained supply tightness—conditions that benefit domestic U.S. refiners by reducing global competition and pushing product prices higher relative to crude costs. With storage inventories still modest (diesel particularly tight), the sector is priced for continued scarcity.
